content.user_title: Evaluate LLM Applications with Measurable Quality
content.value_statement: LLM teams need evidence before changing prompts, models, or retrieval flows. This skill guides automated metrics, judge reviews, human labels, A/B tests, and regression checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains automated metrics such as BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, toxicity, factuality, and groundedness.
Shows LLM-as-judge patterns for single-output scoring and pairwise comparison.
Defines human evaluation forms with annotation dimensions and issue labels.
Demonstrates A/B testing with statistical significance and effect size calculations.
Shows regression detection against baseline results.
Outlines benchmark execution and aggregated metric reporting.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not a complete packaged evaluation library.
Requires users to supply datasets, gold answers, model clients, and domain-specific metrics.
LLM-as-judge results can inherit model bias and need calibration.
Referenced support files are not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Compare prompt changes
use_cases.description: Measure whether a prompt revision improves accuracy, helpfulness, and clarity before release.

use_cases.title: Validate product quality
use_cases.description: Define launch gates that combine automated scores, human review, and baseline comparisons.

use_cases.title: Catch model regressions
use_cases.description: Track evaluation scores over time and identify quality drops after model, prompt, or data changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Evaluation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new LLM feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define an evaluation plan for my LLM feature. Include metrics, test data, baselines, and human review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Task Metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Select metrics for a known LLM task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend automated and human evaluation metrics for this LLM task: [describe task]. Explain when each metric is useful and where it can fail.

prompt_templates.title: Design Regression Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Add release checks to an existing application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a regression evaluation workflow for my existing LLM application. Include baseline storage, thresholds, failure triage, and release gates.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Experiment Protocol
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison across models or prompts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced evaluation protocol comparing two model versions with LLM-as-judge, human calibration, A/B testing, and statistical analysis.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer support chatbot before launch.
output: A metric set covering correctness, relevance, tone, safety, and resolution quality.
A human review plan with rating dimensions and issue labels.
A release gate based on baseline comparison and regression thresholds.

output_examples.input: Compare two prompts for a RAG search assistant.
output_examples.output: A pairwise plan with groundedness scoring, retrieval quality checks, judge calibration, and a regression gate.

output_examples.input: Investigate a drop in summarization quality.
output: A baseline comparison across ROUGE, semantic similarity, and human clarity ratings.
A failure analysis plan for hallucinations, missing facts, and style drift.

best_practices: Use representative examples that reflect production traffic and known failure modes.
Combine automated metrics with calibrated human review for subjective quality dimensions.
Keep baselines and thresholds versioned so prompt and model changes are comparable.
anti_patterns: Relying on one metric for every task and release decision.
Testing only easy examples or samples from training data.
Treating LLM judge scores as objective without calibration or spot checks.

faq.question: Does this skill run evaluations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides evaluation patterns and example implementations that users adapt to their own systems.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-neutral and can support workflows in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What evaluation methods does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers automated metrics, LLM-as-judge review, human annotation, A/B testing, regression checks, and benchmarking.

faq.question: Does it include datasets or runnable scripts?
faq.answer: No. The package contains the SKILL.md guide. Users must provide datasets, model clients, and execution code.

faq.question: Is LLM-as-judge enough for production decisions?
faq.answer: No. Judge outputs should be calibrated with human review and checked against known failure cases.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: ML engineers, AI product managers, and QA teams can use it to make model changes measurable.
